topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, frames the cancer lecture series, and outlines the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Etiology and the Interplay of Chance and Environment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual basis of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease influenced by both intrinsic cellular processes and external epidemiological risk factors.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenic Initiation, Promotion, and Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how diverse biological, physical, and chemical agents interact with host tissues and cellular pathways to drive cancer initiation and promotional growth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the scientific tools and experimental models used to detect mutagenic signatures and demonstrate the carcinogenicity of suspected agents.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by framing cancer risk within everyday practical decision-making and summarizing the core takeaways.
